loan_vowels.note: RESOLVED (profile.md): in scope. Modern, for English/other loanword sounds (ऍ candra e U+090D, ऑ candra o U+0911). Corrected by Agent 3 (build_glyph_data.py --lang hindi run): this category previously duplicated loan_matras's codepoints (U+0945/U+0949) instead of these independent-vowel letters - profile.md's own prose and this file's own excluded_out_of_scope note (U+090D/0911) already had it right; only this category's characters[] array was wrong.

rare_vowels.note: vocalic L/RR/LL - Sanskrit-loanword tier, near-absent from native Hindi vocabulary

nukta_consonants.note: RESOLVED (profile.md): scope is font-gated (whichever of these the chosen font actually renders - Agent 2 confirms), not restricted by 'how standard/common' the letter is. Also: nukta needs NO recorded stroke at all - synthesize it programmatically as a dot (see profile.md's 'New composition primitives'), only its font glyph outline matters here. ALSO exists as decomposed consonant+U+093C sequences in real text - see profile.md's encoding-duality note; do not assume these precomposed codepoints are the only spelling.

matras.note: 10 core dependent vowel signs. ृ (vocalic R, U+0943) promoted here from rare_matras (RESOLVED, profile.md) given its real everyday frequency (कृष्ण, कृपा, कृत्रिम) - needs a recorded stroke, per-consonant-fusion vs. generic composition unverified against real font shaping (Agent 2's job). None of these have a canonical split/compound decomposition (unlike Malayalam's ൊ/ോ/ൌ) - also unverified.

rare_matras.note: vocalic RR/L/LL matra signs. ृ (vocalic R) moved to the core matras category (RESOLVED, profile.md) - see that category's note.

virama.note: halant - suppresses inherent vowel, also the conjunct-formation trigger

candrabindu.note: RESOLVED (profile.md): recorded in full, no normalization to/from anusvara - phonemically distinct, not an alternate spelling of it.

visarga.note: voiceless aspiration, rare outside direct Sanskrit borrowings

numerals.note: Devanagari digits 0-9. Latin digits are also common in modern Hindi text but are UNIVERSAL_CHARS-shaped (script-independent), not part of this category

native_punctuation.note: RESOLVED (profile.md): danda gets one real recorded stroke; double danda is auto-composed from danda's own stroke (offset by its real advance width), not a separate labeling-set entry - see profile.md's 'New composition primitives'.

rare_marks.note: avagraha (vowel elision, dictionary/poetic use), Om (appears in ordinary religious/cultural Hindi text, not just liturgy)

chillu_equivalent.note: Devanagari has no atomic bare-word-final-consonant codepoint the way Malayalam's chillu does - a bare consonant is simply written with an explicit virama and no atomic alternate form

excluded_out_of_scope.note: Deliberately empty of raw glyphs - see codepoints[] below instead. Rationale (per profile.md): these are either Sanskrit/Vedic-only or specific to other Devanagari-using languages (Marwari, Kashmiri, Konkani, Sindhi, Dogri), not Hindi.

codepoints.name: Devanagari Letter Short A
codepoints.reason: not used in Hindi (other-language vowel length distinction)

codepoints.name: Devanagari Letter Short E / Short O
codepoints.reason: other-language letters, not Hindi's loan vowels (those are U+090D/0911 - see loan_vowels)

codepoints.name: Devanagari Vowel Sign Short E / Short O
codepoints.reason: matra forms of the above, same exclusion

codepoints.name: Devanagari Vowel Sign Prishthamatra E / Aw
Devanagari Stress Sign Udatta/Anudatta, Grave/Acute Accent
codepoints.reason: Vedic accent marks - Sanskrit/Vedic-only, reserved for a future Sanskrit profile per profile.md

codepoints.name: Devanagari Vowel Sign Candra Long E / Ue / Uue
Devanagari Letter Candra A, Oe, Ooe, Aw, Ue, Uue, Marwari Dda, Zha, Heavy Ya, Gga, Jja, Glottal Stop, Ddda, Bba
codepoints.reason: added in Unicode 7.0 (2014) specifically for Marwari/Kashmiri/Konkani/Sindhi/Dogri, not Hindi

codepoints.name: (not individually enumerated in this research pass)
codepoints.reason: Vedic accent combining marks for Rigveda-style texts - confirmed to exist and be Sanskrit/Vedic-only, but this pass didn't fetch its per-codepoint chart; do that before treating this exclusion as fully verified

codepoints.name: Devanagari Letter Nnna / Rra / Lla / Llla
codepoints.reason: sit inside the same contiguous U+0915-U+0939 consonant range as Hindi's 33 standard consonants but are Marathi/Dravidian-transliteration letters (ळ Lla is the one most likely to actually surface in a Hindi text, in Marathi-origin loanwords) - not part of the consonants category above

conjunct_hypotheses.status: UNVERIFIED - Agent 2 must confirm or refute each of these against real HarfBuzz shaping before Agent 3 uses any of it

reph.trigger: र (Ra) as the first consonant of a cluster
reph.behavior: renders as a small hook above the end of the syllable, not as standalone र
reph.note: contextual form of an existing atom, not a separate character - open question for Agent 3: composable generically from र's own stroke, or needs its own recording?

rakaar_vattu.trigger: र (Ra) as a non-first consonant of a cluster
rakaar_vattu.behavior: attaches below/after the preceding consonant as a small diagonal stroke

half_forms.trigger: a consonant non-final in a cluster
half_forms.behavior: most consonants have a distinct pre-base 'half form' (vertical stem removed); consonants without one fall back to explicit-halant display
half_forms.note: closest Devanagari analogue to Malayalam's subjoined-conjunct marks, but applies to most of the alphabet rather than a handful of marks - which consonants actually have a distinct half-form glyph in the chosen font is Agent 2's job to enumerate

akhand_ligatures.note: क्ष (kṣa) and ज्ञ (jña) are agreed on almost universally; others vary by source/font. Likely a much shorter list than Malayalam's ~108, but unverified
